fix_assessment.rationale: Culture translation precedes evaluation; a scoped correction is plausible if the locale-specific failure remains reproducible.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve integer operands in power expressions across locales
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Culture translation may transform a comma-decimal or integer argument into syntax the expression engine rejects; verify against the exact locale.
plan: Reproduce integer and decimal operands under reporter locale and en-US.
Trace normalized expression passed to CalculateEngine.Interpret.
Correct the failing translation boundary and add locale-parametrized regression tests.
verification: Verify pow(2,3) and pow(2.5,3) under comma- and dot-decimal locales.
Verify other function calls and ordinary decimal arithmetic remain unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The culture-translation boundary and decimal-separator clue fit, but the failing locale and exact input are missing.

issue_context.summary: Calculator reports Failed to calculate the input for pow(x,y) when x is an integer.
known_information: Report is PowerToys Run 0.84.1 and says it also occurred on 0.85.0.
A commenter said the expression worked with decimal separator dot and could not reproduce it.
Calculator translates input culture before calling CalculateEngine.Interpret.
inferences: The mismatch may be in culture-aware translation or integer argument parsing; the discussion makes locale a useful discriminator.
issue_context.analysis: The decimal-separator follow-up is unresolved. Request exact locale and expression under current version before changing expression normalization.
initial_investigation: Calculator.Query translates and validates input before CalculateEngine.Interpret: src/modules/launcher/Plugins/Microsoft.PowerToys.Run.Plugin.Calculator/Main.cs.

information_gaps.information: Windows number-format locale and decimal separator in effect when the failure occurs.
information_gaps.why_needed: The follow-up says the result changes with a dot separator; locale is needed to reproduce translation.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Share Windows Region format and the decimal separator shown by entering a decimal in Calculator.

information_gaps.information: Exact pow expression with integer x, and whether it succeeds on current PowerToys.
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates integer parsing from locale translation and stale-version behavior.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: In PowerToys Run enter the exact expression, such as =pow(2,3), and report result/error and current version.

comment.body:
Thanks for checking both 0.84.1 and 0.85.0, and for noting that the expression worked with a dot separator. Calculator translates input according to the active number culture. Please confirm:
1. The Windows number-format locale/decimal separator.
2. The exact integer pow expression and whether it fails on the current PowerToys version.
This distinguishes locale conversion from integer argument parsing.
